title: House band at the Cotton Club in Cincinnati
summary: With Leroy Bradley he backed visiting acts and guest bands such as Hines, Duke, Fletcher, Cab and Don Redman, 1933-36; Ben Webster praised his show playing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And I joined the band -- well, after I went to Cincinnati with Leroy Bradley's band, and there we played all the big acts, you know. The Berry Brothers, Ethel Waters, Johnny Hodgins, all the big New York acts would come there.
What was the spot in Cincinnati?
Huh?
What spot was it?
The Cotton Club, it was called.
Oh, yeah. And --
And we used to have, at the Cotton Club,
every week we'd have a guest orchestra, like we would have Earl Hines, Duke, Don Redman.
You were a house band.

We were the house band. But every Friday, Saturday and Sunday, they would invite a band, but we had to play the show. They only played their specialty. And every week we'd have like Earl, Fletcher, Cab.
Lunceford.
Lunceford. Don Redman.
Yeah.
They would all do three days at the Cotton Club. They would be passing through from Chicago.
How long were you house band at that club?
Oh, about three years.
Oh, you got to know everybody then.
Yeah. From 1933 to 1936.
Is that right.

That's when I met Ben, Ben Webster, and he was with Cab, and he says, "Hey, man, the way you play a show, if you ever come to New York you won't have no worries, because they're always looking for somebody to play a show."
Of course it was wonderful experience for you.
There I learned, really, to read music very well.
